solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Believed hype of French rock band making comeback

parts.note: PR, public relations, is promotional hype

indicators.note: coming back means the French word and the band are read backwards together

parts.note: DE is French for 'of'
Muse is an English rock band

explanation.surface: Someone thought a French rock group's return was mostly promotional hype.
explanation.walkthrough: Muse is a British rock band; 'rock band' is the false path towards a word for a stone ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume something is to take it as true without proof, so 'presumed' is a synonym for supposed or believed.

clue.text: Capacious jumper belonging to me

parts.note: a roo (kangaroo) is a jumper
MY means belonging to me

explanation.surface: A roomy sweater that is mine, described by its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater, which is the false path; here it is a kangaroo, a ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roomy has plenty of space inside, which is what capacious means: a synonym.

clue.text: Unexpected loss in stage of competition

parts.note: sudden means unexpected
a death is a loss of life

explanation.surface: A team suffers a shock defeat at some round of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden death is the tie-breaking extra phase of a match where the first score wins, a phase of a contest.

clue.text: Creatures that swim from island advanced on river

parts.note: the Isle of Man
A stands for advanced, as in A level
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Swimming animals travelling from an island and moving up a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Manatees are large aquatic mammals, sea cows, so they are an example of swimming animals.

clue.text: Abroad, used to eating game casserole, a French dish

indicators.note: eating means the rearranged letters take the game, casserole and 'a' inside them
abroad in the sense of widely scattered, so the letters that follow are spread into a new order

parts.note: chess is a board game
a pot is a casserole dish

explanation.surface: Someone used to foreign food tucks into a game stew and a French speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casserole' looks like an anagram signal but is the cooking pot; 'Abroad' rearranges 'used to' into DU...TOES, split around the three eaten pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchess potatoes, pommes duchesse, are piped mashed potato baked until golden, a classic dish of French cuisine.

clue.text: Attendant left on ship? I'm not sure

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
ER is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An unsure speaker wonders whether a steward has been left aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter carries luggage or keeps a door, a kind of attendant or servant.

clue.text: Exercise class on grass lifting small ball

parts.note: PE is physical education at school

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to grass, in British slang, is to inform on someone, to tell

explanation.surface: A PE lesson out on the field throwing a small ball in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns TELL upside down in the down entry to give LLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a tiny compressed round mass, such as shot for an air gun.

clue.text: Drive down slope without parking

indicators.note: without means the letter for parking is left out of the slope

parts.note: a ramp is a slope
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Instructions to drive down an incline where there is nowhere to park.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram something is to force or hammer it down, as with ramming earth or a charge into a gun.

clue.text: Associates in hospital ward as old as us

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
someone as old as us is our age

explanation.surface: Colleagues sharing a hospital ward with patients of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of companions or hangers-on who accompany someone important.

clue.text: Against crossing road over barrier

indicators.note: crossing means the word for against straddles the other letters

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a barrier being put up over a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in as O then RD: C + ORD + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon is a line of police or tape that blocks off an area, so it is a barrier.

clue.text: Woe of a learner driver before noon stuck in metropolis

indicators.note: stuck in means these letters are put inside the city

parts.note: a metropolis is a city
L is the plate on a learner driver's car
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: A learner driver's misery at being stuck in city traffic before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster bringing great distress, so it stands for woe or misfortune.

clue.text: Pronounced part of fork in river

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the prong word is replaced by one that is said the same

parts.note: a tine is a prong of a fork

explanation.surface: A dinner-table remark about a noticeable bit of a fork, or a river fork.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is the river through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne is a major river of north-east England, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Regularly seen three fellows party with American great

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word three

parts.note: men are fellows
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Three men are often spotted partying with an American, and it's great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly seen' takes the first, third and fifth letters of 'three': TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous means very great in size or impressively good, a near synonym.

clue.text: Reinvented a certain old profession

indicators.note: reinvented means the letters are remade into a new form

explanation.surface: A wry remark that the oldest profession has been made over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain old profession' hints at the oldest profession, but 'profession' alone is the definition, meaning an open statement of belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A profession of faith is a public avowal of it, which is a declaration.

clue.text: Liking second post with number following back

indicators.note: back means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
F is short for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys posting a second letter with a number on the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: S + SEND + NO + F gives SSENDNOF; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness is affection or a liking for someone or something, a synonym.

clue.text: Once more showing a profit after deliveries

indicators.note: after means the profit comes behind the deliveries

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A business is back in the black once its deliveries resume.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of balls, or deliveries, bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something over again is to repeat it, so the phrase means once more or afresh.

clue.text: Cry from bird biting rook's throat

indicators.note: biting means the bird's cry holds the rook letter in its mouth

parts.note: caw is the cry of a crow
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird squawks as it pecks at a rook's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A craw is the crop of a bird or loosely the gullet, so it stands for throat.

clue.text: Viewing device in photos cop enlarged

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A camera gadget seen in blown-up photos of a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the instrument a doctor uses to look into the ear, an example of a viewing instrument.

clue.text: Alien in South Africa is Greek character

indicators.note: in places the alien inside the country code

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: An extra-terrestrial in South Africa turns out to be Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is the sixth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the written sense.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy not totally better, bit old, ultimately

indicators.note: not totally means the final letter is dropped from the word for better

parts.note: to better someone is to outdo them
ate is the past tense of eat, and bit is the past tense of bite

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of old

explanation.surface: An old fogey hasn't quite recovered, and is somewhat elderly in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like recovered from illness but means OUTDO, cut to OUTD.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuddy-duddy used as an adjective means old-fashioned and stuffy, the same as out of date.

clue.text: Mythological figure's bust on dais

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A sculpted bust of a god is set up on a platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a sculpture of a head but signals broken letters; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis is the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth, a legendary character.

clue.text: Large structures of castle hard to renovate

indicators.note: to renovate is to rebuild, so the letters are reconstructed in a new order

explanation.surface: Big buildings, like castles, are difficult to restore.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedrals are the principal churches of dioceses and are typically huge buildings.

clue.text: Fit wires cut at both ends

indicators.note: cut at both ends means the first and last letters are trimmed off

parts.note: cables are wires

explanation.surface: An electrician fits wires that have been trimmed at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or fit to do something, a synonym.

clue.text: Woman last to be brought up in concerning hearing

indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter is raised to the top of the word

parts.note: aural means relating to the ear or hearing

explanation.surface: A woman is the final one to be raised at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to be brought up' moves the L at the end of AURAL to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a woman's given name; crosswords use 'woman' for any female name.

clue.text: Dance buff daughter taking over lead in dance

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: taking over the lead means the first letter of the dance is replaced by the daughter letter

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A dance enthusiast's daughter takes the lead role in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: D replaces the T at the start of TANGO to give DANGO.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time.

clue.text: Exhausted running up and down

indicators.note: running up and down means the word reads the same from top or bottom of the down entry

parts.note: a past-tense slang verb: to do someone in, or just to do them, is to wear them out

explanation.surface: Worn out from running up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to 'do' someone can mean to tire them out: the hike did me.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, 'did' can mean wore out or exhausted, as in 'that climb did me'.

clue.text: Horrible having unused wings, dodo bit lousy

indicators.note: having unused wings means each word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A flightless dodo with useless wings is a rather nasty creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The dodo really did have useless wings, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repulsive, a synonym of horrible.

clue.text: Contacts core of group within range

indicators.note: within means that letter sits inside the range

parts.note: the Andes is a mountain range

indicators.note: core means the central letter of group

explanation.surface: Phone contacts belonging to a central group live inside a certain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodes are electrodes, the terminals through which current flows, so they are electrical contacts.

clue.text: Spooner's alcohol support for piano- maker

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink
a stay is a support or prop

explanation.surface: A piano-maker's prop is propped up by booze, says the absent-minded Reverend.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of WINE STAY gives 'stine way', spelt STEIN WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinway & Sons is a famous American-German firm that builds concert grand pianos.
